label: Created Chaos manuscript
description: Steno recorded lessons in his journal entitled 'Chaos' when he was a student in Copenhagen.

label: Recorded lessons in Chaos
description: Steno recorded lessons in his journal, entitled 'Chaos', when he was a student in Copenhagen.

label: Wrote Chaos manuscript
description: Steno's oldest known manuscript, entitled 'Chaos', was written in 1659 when he was a student in Copenhagen.

label: Went to study medicine in the Low Countries
description: Steno went to study medicine in the Low Countries in 1661.

sources.quote: When in 1661 he went to study medicine in the Low Countries, he connected with the circle of Dutch savants and curieux, first in the hotbed of radical thinkers that was Amsterdam, then in nearby Leiden.

label: Studied in Leiden
description: Steno and Swammerdam were fellow students and close friends in Leiden from 1661-1663.

sources.quote: Swammerdam and Steno were fellow students and close friends in Leiden from 1661-1663 and then in Paris in 1664, the two sharing a motivation to search for a bridge between natural philosophy and true religion.

label: Moved to Paris
description: Steno joined Swammerdam in Paris in autumn 1664.

sources.quote: In autumn 1664 he joined Swammerdam in Paris, where, for nearly a year, both were hosted by Melchisédec Thévenot (1620-1692).

label: Public dissection of human brain
description: Steno performed a public dissection of a human brain in Paris in October 1665.

sources.quote: Ferdinand II and Prince Leopold recognized him as an outstanding natural philospher, an anatomist whose public dissection of a human brain performed in Paris in October, 1665 proved Descartes wrong about the manner in which this organ functions.

label: Arrived in Tuscany
description: Steno arrived in Tuscany in April 1666.

sources.quote: Steno arrived in Tuscany in April 1666.

label: Completed Canis Carchariae
description: Steno completed the essay Canis Carchariae Dissectum Caput by December 1666.

description: Canis Carchariae was published in April 1667 as an appendix to his treatise on myology.

sources.quote: This essay was subsequently published in April 1667 as an appendix to his treatise on myology.

label: Published Elementorum Myologiae Specimen
description: Steno's treatise on myology was published in 1667.

label: Completed Prodromus
description: The final text of the Prodromus was completed in August 1668.

sources.quote: The final text was completed in August 1668 after months of additional fieldwork traveling 'from the Arno to the Tiber' (that is, from Florence to Rome: he apparently never suceeded in moving farther south).
The theory was published in its most complete form in the so-called Prodromus of 1669.

label: Visited quarries in Hungary
description: Steno visited quarries in Hungary (present day Slovakia) in October 1669.

sources.quote: In the same year of the publication of the Prodromus, Steno continued to carry out geological fieldwork in the light of his theory, as testified by a letter written in October 1669 after visiting quarries in Hungary (present day Slovakia), a new occasion to study the rocks produced during the time of the first 'universal fluid'.
